absent: Reservation-map representation and need assessment internals beyond commit wrapper behavior
Subpool lifecycle, file binding and quota initialization beyond per-area lookup and get accounting
Global huge-state creation, sizing, surplus limits and buddy allocation internals
Folio reference, poisoning, pinning and free-path accounting contracts
NUMA policy mode values, nodemask derivation and interleave offset helpers
Hugetlb controller enablement, counter layout, limit setting and notification file semantics
Architecture huge-entry adaptation, access-flag update and translation-cache maintenance
Mapping lock, interval-tree walk, notifier ranges and translation-gather lifecycle

findings.text: Allocation interface for huge folios at a fault address. The per-area entry consumes or commits reservations and applies caller NUMA placement, returning either a folio linked to the area subpool or an error pointer for exhaustion or quota failure. The lower entry performs controller admission and pool selection, while the buddy entry creates surplus capacity honoring preferred-many fallback. All three report space exhaustion on failure.

Hugetlb controller interface for admission and ownership. Charge entries attempt regular or reserved accounting for a size class and return status with an output group reference. Commit entries attach a previously charged group to a live folio. Uncharge entries release a charge that was never committed. Lookup helpers resolve the group for the current task or from a subsystem state.

Memory-management helpers visible outside the local unit. Policy helpers resolve effective NUMA policy and preferred node for huge faults. Unmap helpers clear huge ranges with notifier coverage and adjust the notified interval when table sharing is possible, with a no-op build variant. Fault-hash helpers map a mapping plus index to a mutex selector, with a single-mutex build variant. Additional entries prepare anonymous tracking for faults and copy user data across large folios.

Reservation outcome determines quota and accounting obligations. Copy from owner uses an enforced outcome that bypasses per-area map consumption and skips later commit and termination handling. A needed outcome indicates no prior per-area reservation and requires subpool quota acquisition together with reserved controller accounting. A reuse outcome indicates an existing reservation and allows use of global reservations without extra global charging.

Lower-level allocation moves from admission to selection to publication. Admission obtains regular and optionally reserved controller budget. Selection reuses a preallocated entry when global-reservation use is permitted or spare entries exist, otherwise builds surplus capacity outside the global lock and then publishes it to the active set. Publication optionally consumes one global reservation and records restore intent, attaches controller ownership, and performs memory-controller charging and statistics. Failures before publication unwind controller budget, while memory-controller failure after publication frees the folio and relies on free-path cleanup for committed charges.

Subpool state holds maximum and in-use counts plus minimum and remaining-reserved counts, with a negative sentinel disabling a limit. Global huge state holds free and reserved totals, per-node free counts, per-node free lists and a shared active list. Spare capacity available for fresh use is the excess of free total over reserved total. Per-area subpool identity derives from the area file host.

Subpool limit and reservation counters mutate only while holding the subpool lock. Selection from preallocated lists, linkage to the active set, reference activation and global reservation consumption mutate only while holding the global huge lock. Surplus creation runs without that lock and rejoins it for publication. Controller usage publication also occurs under the global lock.

Preferred-many placement first restricts selection to the policy node set and then retries without restriction when empty. Zonelist scanning for the requested node skips disallowed zones and avoids revisiting the same node, because pooling is node granular, and restarts when the allowed set changes mid-scan. Node-exact draining skips entries incompatible with pinning, entries marked poisoned and entries isolated for migration, and only successful handover moves the entry to the active set with counter updates.

Controller admission is a successful no-op when disabled. Otherwise it repeatedly resolves the caller group until a stable subsystem reference is obtained, then attempts counter charging for the size class and reservation class. Charge failure reports limit excess through hierarchical events and releases the lookup reference. Reserved charges keep their reference until explicitly uncharged because they are not reparented, while ordinary charges drop the lookup reference after a successful attempt. Uncharge reverses the counter and conditionally drops the reserved reference.

Ownership publication is a no-op when the controller is disabled or no group was charged. Otherwise it records the group on the folio, distinguishing ordinary from reserved ownership. Ordinary publication additionally adds the huge size to per-node usage for the folio node and size class. Reserved publication records reservation ownership without usage mutation.

Limit notification updates a local tally and file at the originating group and then walks parents updating hierarchical tallies and files, stopping the walk at the root so the root parent is not notified twice.

Effective NUMA policy prefers area operation policy when the area provides one, else area policy, else task policy. Interleave variants advance the supplied offset by area start and by fault displacement, both scaled from base to huge granularity. The caller then derives a preferred node and optional node set from the resolved policy and offset.

New huge entries derive protection from the folio and area, allow write with dirty only when explicitly requested and the area permits writing, otherwise enforce write protection, always mark youth, and then apply architecture adaptation for huge size and area flags. Installed entries can later be promoted to writable, either unconditionally or guarded by area writability, with translation-cache refresh performed only when access-flag update indicates a change.

External huge unmapping surrounds internal clearing with invalidation start and end notifications and a translation-gather lifetime. When the area is shared and spans at least one aligned compound-table unit overlapped by the request, the notified bounds expand outward to unit alignment to cover potential sharing. A configuration without sharing implements the adjustment as having no effect.

Private-reference invalidation aligns the fault location to huge size, maps it to a file offset in the shared file, and visits every area mapping that offset while holding the mapping write lock. It leaves the triggering area and all shared areas untouched and clears the huge extent from other private areas that lack owner reservation, so stale private mappings cannot later observe replaced contents.

Fault-mutex selection combines mapping identity with page index through a general hash and then restricts the result to the configured mutex count. A reduced configuration always selects the same single mutex.

Fault preparation for anonymous areas returns immediately when tracking already exists. Otherwise it obtains address-space read protection with retry behavior when invoked under area locking, attempts to allocate tracking with allocation failure mapped to an out-of-memory fault outcome, and releases protection acquired in this path.

User copying for large folios routes extremely large instances to a gigantic handler and otherwise iterates constituent base units in a hint-centric order that preserves locality of the hinted unit by visiting it last, cooperates with the scheduler during long walks, and stops at the first failing unit propagating its status.

Concurrent reservation between need assessment and commit can turn a needed outcome into already-reserved; the allocator detects that transition and rolls back the speculative subpool quota, global accounting and reserved controller charge. Undo on allocation failure returns subpool quota only when quota was taken without consuming a prior global reservation, and reservation termination is skipped for the enforced copy path. Pool draining must exclude poisoned, migration-isolated and pin-incompatible entries.

Interpreted placement passed to the allocator bundles a resolved node, an effective mode that falls back to a default when policy is absent or NUMA support is unavailable, and an optional node-set pointer. Controller state organizes budgets and events per huge size class, with local and hierarchical event tallies plus notification files, and per-node usage tables indexed by size class.

Node-exact draining and controller commit both require the caller to already hold the global huge lock, enforced by a held-lock assertion. Per-node usage read-modify-write relies on that exclusion rather than atomicity.
